questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language, culture, history and academic opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite tough to figure out which modules I could enroll in. Otherwise, the necessary information was available.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a week of orientation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find the shared room I ended up living in, but I could not find anything else.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived with other exchange students and that was mostly fine, except people do not move out from their parents at the same time in all countries, and my roommate did not know how to live on his own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is quite easy to enroll in modules, but quite difficult to know which you are eligible for.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: During the orientation week there was an online meeting on the sociological modules I could enroll in. As it turned out I did not get any courses with more than 5 ECTS points meaning I had to take courses in Philosophy, Theology an elective and 6 courses in total.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Sorry, but the coordinator was not of much help. My fellow studen from Copenhagen and I figured it out together.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 2 of the 4 modules I had read about and knew I wanted to get into.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not expect to be enrolled in the modules you read about from home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is a little bit easier than in Copenhagen, but any language barrier might make up for it. A few of the classes I took had a bit of repetition from the classes I have taken in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I do not think the style of teaching was that different from that of UCPH.
There are more presentations in Trinity in the exercise classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

Additional comments:
questions.answer: I sought out activities outside of Trinity. I frequented a boxing club in Stoneybatter.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts of social clubs, sports clubs and debate clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I do not partake in many non-academic activities at UCPH either so I am not the right respondent on this matter. 
My advice is to go on plenty of long walks around the city. Go hear some music at the Cobblestone and grab a pint. Read about the rich history of Dublin and go out and see it for yourself. Attend some comedy shows or a concert at 3arena. Find some random people in a pub and talk to them. I generally just went out on my own and was rarely bored.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
My advice is to go on plenty of long walks around the city. Go hear some music at the Cobblestone and grab a pint. Read about the rich history of Dublin and go out and see it for yourself. Attend some comedy shows or a concert at 3arena. Find some random people in a pub and talk to them. I generally just went out on my own and was rarely bored. 
Of course the academic stuff is important, but you have to go experience Dublin and its culture.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Real easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not really do that outside of the classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You should just be aware that religion and history is no joke in Ireland. People have strong feelings about catholics/protestants, the Irish/the Northern Irish, the British, poverty and immigration and these subjects are no joking matter... most of the time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I found it all very interesting. Historywise, I delved into the Easter Rising and James Connolly. I also went to Belfast during 'Reading Week' and learned a lot about the troubles and the current state of Belfast.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. You cannot expect to enroll in the modules you read about from home. 
2. Unless you have connections you can expect modest housing
3. Read up on Irish history. It is really worth it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of right now, no.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just to experience the culture. I'm glad to be home amongst friends and family, but I truly miss the streets of Dublin.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be away from my girlfriend and having to share a room.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
